title: Carbon Fibre Pool Refraction Lab
description: A swimming pool scene is overlaid with a carbon fibre panel acting as a post-process filter lens. The user adjusts bloom, chromatic aberration, vignette, tone-mapping exposure, and saturation through coupled sliders while toggling the carbon fibre overlay opacity. An energy-conservation law links bloom intensity inversely to vignette strength, and all changes support full undo/redo.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) with EffectComposer, RenderPass, UnrealBloomPass, and ShaderPass. Load pool.glb as the main scene object centered at origin and CarbonFibre.glb positioned as a flat panel 0.5 units in front of the camera, acting as a translucent overlay lens. Use a PerspectiveCamera at (0,3,6) looking at origin, with OrbitControls. Add one DirectionalLight and one AmbientLight. Post-processing chain: RenderPass → UnrealBloomPass → custom ShaderPass for chromatic aberration, vignette, saturation, and a carbon-fibre opacity uniform that alpha-blends the carbon fibre panel's rendered texture onto the final output using a second render target. Create a UI panel with 6 sliders: (1) Bloom Intensity 0-3, (2) Chromatic Aberration Offset 0-0.02, (3) Vignette Darkness 0-2, (4) Exposure 0.1-3, (5) Saturation 0-2, (6) Carbon Overlay Opacity 0-1. Enforce an energy conservation law: bloom + vignette must sum to a constant 2.5; adjusting one auto-corrects the other. Changing exposure must proportionally scale saturation (multi-input coupling) unless the user unlocks them via a toggle button. Implement an undo/redo system storing snapshots of all 6 values plus the coupling lock state. Bind Ctrl+Z for undo and Ctrl+Y for redo, and also show Undo/Redo buttons. The task requires 10-14 steps: load scene, set bloom to 1.5, observe vignette auto-adjust, set chromatic aberration to 0.01, increase carbon overlay to 0.7, adjust exposure to 2.0 and observe saturation coupling, unlock coupling, independently set saturation to 0.5, undo twice to restore coupled state, redo once, set vignette to 1.0 and observe bloom conservation, then set final overlay opacity to 0.3. Display current parameter values in a HUD. Renderer should use toneMapping = ACESFilmicToneMapping with toneMappingExposure driven by the exposure slider.
